title: 2023 HMMT November General Problem 4
statement: Suppose that \(a\) and \(b\) are real numbers such that the line \(y=a x+b\) intersects the graph of \(y=x^{2}\) at two distinct points \(A\) and \(B\). If the coordinates of the midpoint of \(A B\) are \((5,101)\), compute \(a+b\).

solutions.text:
As in the previous solution, let \(A=\left(r, r^{2}\right)\) and \(B=\left(s, s^{2}\right)\) and note \(r+s=10=a\).
Fixing \(a=10\), the \(y\)-coordinate of the midpoint is 50 when \(b=0\) (and changing \(b\) shifts the line up or down by its value). So, increasing \(b\) by 51 will make the midpoint have \(y\)-coordinate \(50+51=101\), so the answer is \(10+51=61\).
